title: Derived base change of a relatively flat closed kernel in a product
statement:
Let $S_0$ be a scheme, let $X_0,Y_0$ be $S_0$-schemes, and let $a:S\to S_0$ be any scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Put $T_0=X_0\times_{S_0}Y_0$, $T=T_0\times_{S_0}S$, and write $q:T\to T_0$ for the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $i_0:W_0\hookrightarrow T_0$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that $Y_0\to S_0$ and the composite $W_0\xrightarrow{i_0}T_0\to X_0$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Form $W=W_0\times_{T_0}T$ with closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow T$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$Lq^*((i_{0,*}\mathcal O_{W_0})[0])\simeq(i_*\mathcal O_W)[0]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_T)$$
[def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-module-pullback]. No flatness of $a$, of $X_0\to S_0$, or of $i_0$, and no Noetherian or finiteness hypotheses are assumed.

proof.text: Put $X=X_0\times_{S_0}S$ and let $b:X\to X_0$ be its projection. The fibre-product universal property identifies $T$ with $T_0\times_{X_0}X$: giving either object means giving maps to $X_0,Y_0,S$ with their three maps to $S_0$ equal. Likewise $W\simeq W_0\times_{X_0}X$. The projection $p:T_0\to X_0$ is the base change of $Y_0\to S_0$, hence flat. The morphism $i:W\to T$ is a closed immersion by closed-immersion base change.

Apply the common-base flat-families Tor-independence lemma with base $X_0$, source $W_0$, target $T_0$, morphism $i_0$, and base extension $b:X\to X_0$. Its two flatness hypotheses are precisely the given flatness of $W_0\to X_0$ and the flatness of $p$ from step 1. The target base change is $T$, so it says exactly that $i_0$ and $q:T\to T_0$ are stalkwise Tor independent. This is the application of Tag 0CTA; neither $b$ nor $i_0$ is assumed flat.

Apply the Tor-independent closed-pushforward comparison to the cartesian square $(W,W_0,T,T_0)$ with $K=\mathcal O_{W_0}[0]$. Step 2 supplies Tor independence and $i_0$ is closed by hypothesis. It gives the canonical isomorphism $Lq^*Ri_{0,*}(\mathcal O_{W_0}[0])\simeq Ri_*Lr^*(\mathcal O_{W_0}[0])$, where $r:W\to W_0$ is projection.

Derived pullback of the degree-zero structure sheaf is the degree-zero structure sheaf, so $Lr^*(\mathcal O_{W_0}[0])\simeq\mathcal O_W[0]$. For each of the closed immersions $i_0,i$, module pushforward preserves homology. Thus it preserves acyclic complexes and its derived functor is its termwise functor; on a degree-zero complex it is the degree-zero ordinary pushforward. Substituting these identifications in step 3 gives the asserted isomorphism. It is canonical: use the base-change adjoint specified in that comparison and the tensor-unit pullback identification $1\otimes s\mapsto s$; exact pushforward uses the identity on representatives. Every identification works for arbitrary $a$.
